text:
sara (support): FYI AcmeCorp is seeing mass 401s starting ~12:03 UTC after our scheduled credential rotation. They reported their webhooks and background jobs failing.

sara (support): customer pasted a sample error: 
```
{"error":"unauthorized","message":"Invalid credentials: token has insufficient scope"}
```

sara (support): cURL repro they ran:
```
curl -i -H \"Authorization: Bearer <redacted>\" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
content-type: application/json
{\n  \"error\": \"unauthorized\",\n  \"code\": \"unauthorized.scope\"\n}
```

alex (customer-success): P1 for the customer, they're losing revenue. They said this started right after the nightly rotation job. Requesting ETA for mitigation.

jason (eng-runtime): On it. Can someone paste the rotation job run id? Looking for any prune/cleanup flags.

deploy-bot: deployment 2026-11-02T11:58:12Z rotated-keys-job v2.3.1 -> SUCCESS (run_id=run_20261102115812)

kai (eng-sre): Pulling logs from keysync and auth-service now. Noting spikes in 401s in frontends and gateway.

maria (security): Any change to token scopes or default scopes in this release? We didn't intend to shrink scopes. Also: were service-account tokens re-issued or just user API keys?

jason (eng-runtime): rotation job re-issued both user API keys and service account tokens. The job has a prune flag that removes old tokens after sync. I see a recent commit that tweaked the svc-account filter. Pushing log snippet.

kai (eng-sre): Logs showing auth-service rejecting tokens from internal services with cause field: 
```
[auth] reject token=svc-acme-batcher reason=missing_scope required=[api:write webhooks:deliver]
```

jason (eng-runtime): Hmm. The new rotation script accidentally generated tokens with scopes [api:read] for any service-account matching `svc-*` due to a defaulting bug in the scope-merger. That explains the insufficient scope error.

sara (support): Customer workaround requested: can we issue a temporary token with the expected scopes and share via secure channel? They need to be unblocked ASAP.

maria (security): We can issue short-lived emergency token (scoped) but want to avoid broad supertokens. Recommend issuing token with explicit scopes and TTL 1 hour.

jason (eng-runtime): I can issue per-customer emergency token and patch the rotation job. Quick mitigation steps I'm going to run now: 1) revoke faulty tokens for affected svc-ids, 2) issue emergency tokens with correct scopes, 3) patch rotation script to respect scope defaults.

kai (eng-sre): I'm placing an autoscaling cooldown to reduce noisy retries and to prevent cascading failures. Also creating a Prometheus alert for >2% 401 rate in prod gateway.

alex (customer-success): Customer has accepted emergency token approach. Please share how we revoke after stability.

jason (eng-runtime): Action log: 
- Issued scoped emergency token for svc-acme-batcher (ttl=3600s) and provided to CS through secure vault.
- Rolled back prune step for rotation job (disabled prune flag) to keep old tokens available until we finish reconciliation.
- Pushed hotfix to rotation script: ensure scope inheritance: `scope = requested || default_service_scope` (fix in PR #4892).

jason (eng-runtime): Hotfix deployed canary to staging then to one region in prod. Monitoring 401s now.

deploy-bot: deployment 2026-11-02T12:14:37Z rotation-job hotfix v2.3.2 -> SUCCESS (run_id=run_20261102121437)

kai (eng-sre): 12:20 UTC gateway 401 rate dropped from 18% -> 1.2% in the affected region after rollback + emergency tokens. CPU and latency stable.

maria (security): Confirmed emergency token TTL and audit log entry recorded. Will follow up with KMS audit to verify key provenance.

sara (support): Customer confirmed webhooks are back, background jobs resumed. They asked for a root cause summary and compensation guidance.

jason (eng-runtime): Root cause analysis (brief): rotation job's scope-merge logic had a regression introduced in PR #4860 where service-account scope defaults were overwritten by a nil fallback to [api:read]. The prune step removed legacy tokens quickly, leaving services with under-privileged tokens.

jason (eng-runtime): Repro steps for engineers: 
1) Run local rotation emulation against a test tenant and sample service account with no explicit scope set.
2) Observe issuance of tokens with [api:read] instead of default `[api:write, webhooks:deliver]`.
3) Run rotation job with `--disable-prune` to confirm tokens remain valid until reconciliation.

jason (eng-runtime): Example failing unit test we added: 
```
# ensure default scopes preserved
old = {name: 'svc-x', scopes: nil}
res = rotate(old)
assert res.scopes == ['api:write','webhooks:deliver']
```

maria (security): Post-incident actions: 
- Revert prune by default until we have a successful canary for 24h.
- Add scope-preservation integration tests in the rotation pipeline.
- Require a manual security review for any rotation-related code changes.

kai (eng-sre): Operational actions: 
- Add a Canary target: rotate one internal non-critical svc and validate 24h of no regressions before global rollout.
- Add alert for >1% 401s aggregated across customer-facing endpoints.
- Backfill metrics for last 30 days and notify customers who exceeded error budgets.

sara (support): Billing impact: some customers hit retry loops, causing bursts. @billing-bot can you estimate potential overage credits exposure for AcmeCorp?

billing-bot: Estimated token consumption spike for AcmeCorp during incident window: +2.3% billable tokens. Recommend manual credit of storm usage per CS playbook.

alex (customer-success): I'll coordinate credit + message. CS will send post-incident summary and offer handoff call.

jason (eng-runtime): Long-term fixes queued in sprint: 
- PRs: #4892 (hotfix), #4901 (integration tests), #4910 (canary orchestration).
- Add a CI job to simulate multi-tenant rotation and validate scopes.

maria (security): Also adding an audit rule: any token rotation that reduces scope (vs previous token) must flag for manual approval.

sara (support): Thanks team. I'll update the customer and close the P1 once CS confirms acceptance.

kai (eng-sre): Leaving a small checklist for the oncall: 
- Confirm rotation job runs with prune disabled for 24h.
- Monitor 401 alert and escalate if >1% for >10m.
- Ensure emergency tokens are revoked after TTL.

sara (support): CS confirmed. Closing incident once we revoke emergency tokens and patch is in stable for 24h. :white_check_mark:

alex (customer-success): Customer happy with fast turnaround. Requesting a joint postmortem doc with timeline and affected customers list.

jason (eng-runtime): Will draft postmortem. ETA EOD.

maria (security): I'll add compliance notes and KMS audit export to the postmortem.

sara (support): Great work. Filing follow-up tasks in the infra board.

kai (eng-sre): Oncall handoff in 30m, will keep monitoring for 2 hours then hand off.

sara (support): Thanks everyone.
